result.summary: The environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane roadway with industrial-scale buildings and significant crossing distances. While sidewalks are present and wide, the lack of physical traffic calming and faded pavement markings create a high-speed feel that is less than ideal for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a long duration without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk on the right side of the intersection is significantly worn, reducing its visibility to drivers.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Cut
hazards.description: A large, undefined vehicle access point to a parking area creates a broad conflict zone for pedestrians on the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, entrance to the parking lot

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Remark the crossing with continental or ladder-style markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is poorly defined, lacking a clear curb or physical separation from the roadway. The wide paved area intended for pedestrians is currently obstructed by a parked vehicle, and the surrounding industrial land use features blank frontages and minimal safety infrastructure.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A black SUV is parked directly on the paved walkway area, forcing pedestrians to deviate into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground, parked on the paved apron

hazards.name: Lack of Vertical Separation
hazards.description: There is no raised curb separating the roadway from the pedestrian area, allowing vehicles to easily encroach on the walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the edge of the asphalt roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The large stone wall and billboard structure limit sightlines for pedestrians and drivers near the property edge.

interventions.title: Raised Curb Installation
interventions.description: Install a standard 6-inch vertical curb to physically separate the pedestrian walkway from the travel lanes.

interventions.title: Bollards or Planters
interventions.description: Place bollards or heavy planters along the edge of the walkway to prevent vehicles from parking on the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Wayfinding and Markings
interventions.description: Clearly mark the pedestrian path with paint or different paving materials to distinguish it from vehicle space.

result.summary: The street environment is characterized by an industrial-commercial setting with wide lanes and no marked pedestrian crossings. Pedestrians on the narrow left sidewalk are exposed to traffic with no buffer, while large parked vehicles on the right create significant sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks forces pedestrians to judge gaps in traffic across a wide roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large commercial truck parked at the curb blocks the view of oncoming traffic for pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install bold, continental-style crosswalk markings to improve driver awareness and pedestrian safety.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at intersections or mid-block to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between users.

result.summary: The image depicts a multi-lane roadway with a mid-block yellow-marked crosswalk that lacks signalization or a refuge island. The environment is characterized by industrial land use, blank frontages, and parked vehicles that create visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Mid-block Crossing
hazards.description: A wide, multi-lane crossing without signals or a median refuge island increases pedestrian exposure to high-speed traffic.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and dense vegetation on the far side of the street block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The presence of a vacant lot and a windowless mural wall reduces natural surveillance and can make the environment feel less safe for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by 'daylighting' the intersection.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add user-actuated amber LEDs to the crossing to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.
